issues.t: Brake control unit corrosion reduces braking (recall)
issues.sym: The brake pedal feels soft or sinks further than usual, stopping takes longer, or the ABS and brake warning lights come on.
issues.why: The factory brake fluid did not protect the hydraulic electronic control unit (the ABS/stability control pump and valve block) from internal corrosion. Corroded valves can reduce braking force. Hyundai recalled sedans built through March 2012 and later extended coverage on this unit to 15 years with unlimited miles.
issues.next: If the brake pedal suddenly turns hard or a red brake warning comes on, press the pedal much harder than normal, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — call for a tow. Treat any soft pedal as urgent and do not drive the car until it is checked. Ask a Hyundai dealer to run your VIN for recall 13V-489 and the control unit warranty extension.

issues.t: ABS module can short and catch fire (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning at all. Some owners notice a burning smell, smoke from under the hood, or the ABS light coming on, even with the car parked.
issues.why: Brake fluid can leak inside the anti-lock brake module and cause an electrical short, which can start a fire in the engine bay while driving or parked. This covers 2011-2015 Genesis Coupes and 2015-2016 Genesis sedans.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: if you smell burning or see smoke, pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off, get everyone out and well away from the car, and call 911 if there are flames. Don't drive it again until it has been repaired. Park outside and away from buildings until the fix is done. Check your VIN for recalls 23V-651 (Coupe) or 21V-160 (sedan); the dealer installs a new fuse for free.

issues.t: Brake lights may not work (recall)
issues.sym: Brake lights stay off when you press the pedal, cruise control will not switch off with the brake, the shifter can move out of Park without pressing the brake, or the push-button start acts up.
issues.why: The brake light switch can fail internally, and on some sedans the brake light circuit itself can fail. Hyundai recalled the switch on 2009-2011 sedans and 2010-2011 Coupes, and separately repaired the stop lamp circuit on 2009-2011 sedans.
issues.next: Have someone confirm your brake lights work. Check your VIN for recalls 13V-113 and 14V-713; both repairs are free.

issues.t: Engine shuts off while driving at low speed
issues.sym: The engine suddenly cuts out, often at low speed or while turning, and the steering and brakes become heavy. It usually restarts, and often no warning light or code is stored.
issues.why: No single cause has been confirmed. Owners and dealers have traced some cases to loose or corroded battery terminals and power connections, a failed engine-bay fuse box, or sensors, and many dealers could not reproduce it.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. If it happens, steer and brake firmly to a safe stop and restart in Park. Have the battery terminals, main power leads and fuse box checked first, and keep a log of when it happens to help the shop.

issues.t: Engine knocking or seized engine
issues.sym: A deep knocking from the engine that gets louder with speed, low oil pressure warnings, or the engine locking up and stopping.
issues.why: Owners report engines failing from internal wear, and Hyundai issued a service bulletin on testing connecting rod bearing clearance for these years. Low oil level or long oil-change intervals make bearing damage more likely.
issues.next: Stop driving if you hear a new knock or see the oil light. Check the oil level, and ask a dealer whether the rod bearing bulletin or a warranty applies before paying for a new engine.

issues.t: Excessive oil consumption
issues.sym: You need to add oil between changes, or the low oil pressure light comes on before the next service.
issues.why: Some 2012 owners report the engine burning oil faster than normal. Running the engine low on oil can damage bearings over time.
issues.next: Check the dipstick every few fill-ups and keep a record. If it uses more than about a quart every 1,000-2,000 miles, ask the dealer for an oil consumption test.

issues.t: Harsh or delayed shifts (8-speed automatic)
issues.sym: Jerky or thumping upshifts, a flare in engine speed between gears, a delay when shifting into Drive or Reverse, or a sudden hard shift when accelerating.
issues.why: The 8-speed automatic relies on learned clutch pressure data. Hyundai released several service bulletins with software updates and pressure data reprogramming to smooth the 2-3, 3-4 and 4-5 shifts and fix delayed engagement.
issues.next: Ask a dealer to check for and apply the latest transmission software updates. If it slips or shows a gear ratio code, get a full transmission diagnosis.

issues.t: Shudder or rough shifting (6-speed automatic)
issues.sym: A shudder during light acceleration around 50-60 mph, a harsh shift out of Park, the shifter refusing to leave Park, or clunky, slapping shifts.
issues.why: Hyundai issued service bulletins for these early Genesis sedans with transmission computer updates to reduce shudder and clutch-wear compensation, plus a fix for harsh or no shift out of Park.
issues.next: Have a dealer check for the transmission software updates. Check the fluid level and condition, especially on higher-mileage cars.

issues.t: Battery keeps going dead
issues.sym: The car will not start after sitting a few days, even with a new battery.
issues.why: Something keeps drawing power after the car is shut off. Owners report dealers blaming a faulty radio or a loose wiring connection that kept the alarm system awake.
issues.next: Ask a shop for a parasitic draw test, which measures current with the car off and pulls fuses one at a time to find the circuit that is draining the battery.

issues.t: No sound from the speakers
issues.sym: The radio and navigation screen work, but sound cuts out from all speakers, sometimes on and off.
issues.why: Hyundai issued a bulletin to replace the Lexicon premium audio amplifier for intermittent sound loss, and RepairPal notes the problem on navigation-equipped cars.
issues.next: Have a dealer check whether the amplifier bulletin applies to your car before replacing the head unit.

issues.t: Idle speed surges when cold
issues.sym: The idle speed rises and falls when the engine is cold, the engine may run rough, and the check engine light can come on.
issues.why: Hyundai issued bulletins replacing the throttle position sensor and updating the engine computer for cold-engine idle fluctuation and throttle sensor codes.
issues.next: Have the codes read and ask the dealer about the throttle sensor and engine computer updates.

issues.t: Rough idle or stalling from a dirty throttle body
issues.sym: Rough or hunting idle, stalling at stops, hard starting when cold, or a check engine light with an idle control code.
issues.why: Carbon builds up in the throttle body and intake on the direct-injection V6, which can upset idle control. Some owners needed throttle body replacement and engine computer updates.
issues.next: Ask a shop to clean the throttle body and relearn the idle. If codes keep returning, have it checked for a failing throttle body and software updates.

issues.t: Windshield wipers stop working (recall)
issues.sym: The wipers work only on and off, or stop completely.
issues.why: A seal on the wiper motor cover can break down and let water corrode the motor's circuit board. Hyundai recalled 2012 Genesis sedans built through April 2012.
issues.next: Do not drive in rain or snow without working wipers. Check your VIN for recall 16V-117.

issues.t: Clear coat peeling and paint chipping
issues.sym: Clear coat peeling or yellowing on the bumpers and rocker panels (often on white sedans), or large chips flaking off the hood and roof on Coupes.
issues.why: Owners describe the paint layers separating, with problems showing up around 30,000-80,000 miles and sometimes returning after repainting.
issues.next: Photograph the damage and ask a dealer about paint warranty or goodwill. Get a repaint quote from a body shop that guarantees its work.

issues.t: Sudden loss of all electrical power or no start
issues.sym: The car goes completely dead, the clock and settings reset after shutting off, or it will not crank even though the lights may work.
issues.why: Owners and dealers found loose battery terminal screws and a loose power lead nut at the under-hood fuse block. A few cases were traced to an aftermarket alarm or a failed engine computer.
issues.next: Have the battery terminals and main fuse block connections checked and tightened before replacing parts. Remove any aftermarket alarm if problems started after it was installed.

issues.t: Starter solenoid can short and catch fire (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning. Some cars may show starting problems, a burning smell or smoke from the engine bay.
issues.why: Water can get into the starter solenoid and cause a short circuit, which can lead to an engine compartment fire.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: if you smell burning or see smoke, pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off, get everyone out and well away from the car, and call 911 if there are flames. Don't drive it again until it has been repaired. Park outside and away from buildings until repaired. Check your VIN for recall 24V-107; dealers add a relay kit for free.

issues.t: Power seat motor can overheat (recall)
issues.sym: A front power seat keeps moving or will not stop, a burning or electrical smell, or smoke from under a front seat.
issues.why: If a front seat control switch sticks, the seat motor can keep running and overheat, which can start a fire.
issues.next: If a seat keeps moving on its own, stop and turn the car off. Check your VIN for recall 26V-664 and park outside and away from other cars until the remedy is done.

issues.t: Parking brake warning light may not come on (recall)
issues.sym: The parking brake light does not come on even though the parking brake is partly set, so you may drive with it dragging, which can cause a burning smell and worn brakes.
issues.why: The parking brake switch can corrode and stop telling the dash the brake is applied.
issues.next: Make sure the parking brake is fully released before driving. Check your VIN for recall 17V-359.

issues.t: Instrument cluster shows wrong speed or warning lights (recall)
issues.sym: The 7-inch cluster shows the wrong speed, lights up every warning light at once, or fails to show a warning when it should.
issues.why: A software fault in the instrument cluster on sedans built February-May 2015.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 16V-575; the dealer updates the cluster software for free.

issues.t: Original tires can crack in the sidewall (recall)
issues.sym: Cracks in the sidewalls of the factory tires, a bulge, or a sudden loss of air.
issues.why: Some original Hankook Ventus S1 noble2 tires can develop sidewall cracks that may lead to a blowout.
issues.next: Inspect the tire sidewalls. If your car still has these tires, check your VIN for recall 15V-864; dealers replace them with another brand for free.

issues.t: Water in tail lights causes wrong gear display (recall)
issues.sym: The dash shows the wrong gear, the car is slow to go into gear, or it may move when you do not expect it.
issues.why: Water can leak into the rear combination lamps and reach wiring that affects the gear display and engagement.
issues.next: Always confirm the car is in Park and set the parking brake. Check your VIN for recall 15V-097.

issues.t: Passenger airbag sensor connector can come loose (recall)
issues.sym: The airbag warning light or passenger airbag status light may act up, often after the passenger seat is moved. (Genesis Coupe.)
issues.why: A connector for the passenger seat occupant sensor can work loose when the seat is moved, so the passenger airbag may deploy with the wrong force in a crash.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 16V-722. Have the airbag light checked if it comes on.

issues.t: Car can move if started in gear (recall)
issues.sym: On manual-transmission Coupes, the engine can start and the car can lurch if it is in gear without the clutch pressed.
issues.why: A return spring in the ignition switch can break, which lets the starter work without the clutch interlock doing its job.
issues.next: Always start the car in neutral with the parking brake set. Check your VIN for recall 24V-562.

issues.t: Rear differential bolts can loosen (recall)
issues.sym: A clunk or vibration from the rear, especially when shifting or taking off, or a sudden loss of drive. (Manual-transmission Coupes.)
issues.why: If the rear differential was misaligned at the factory, its mounting bolts can loosen and the driveshaft can disconnect.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 15V-756 and have the rear differential checked if you hear new clunks.

issues.t: Driver airbag bolts may be loose (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no sign. A rattle from the steering wheel hub is possible. (2016 Coupe.)
issues.why: The driver airbag mounting bolts may not have been tightened enough, so the airbag could come loose from the steering wheel.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 20V-248; dealers retighten the bolts for free.

issues.t: Turbo wastegate actuator failure
issues.sym: Loss of power, boost that will not build or overboost codes, a check engine light, and sometimes a rattle from the turbo.
issues.why: Owners of the 2.0T Coupe report the wastegate actuator arm breaking or the boost control solenoid failing, which can mean a new turbo.
issues.next: Have the boost control system checked. If the actuator arm has broken, stop driving hard so parts do not get pulled into the turbo.

issues.t: Cam timing (CVVT) codes and timing chain wear
issues.sym: Check engine light with cam timing codes such as P0014 or P0017, rough running, rattle on start-up, or the engine cranking but not starting.
issues.why: On the 2.0T Coupe, the cam phasers (CVVT units), timing chain or tensioner can wear or stick, throwing the cam timing out. Dirty or wrong-grade oil makes it worse.
issues.next: Do not ignore cam timing codes. Change the oil with the correct grade and have the timing system inspected before the chain skips.

issues.t: Engine revs hang between shifts
issues.sym: On manual Coupes, engine speed drops slowly after you press the clutch, making shifts jerky.
issues.why: The engine computer holds the throttle open briefly between shifts. Hyundai issued a bulletin with an engine computer reflash.
issues.next: Ask a dealer for the engine computer update.

issues.t: Clutch slave or master cylinder failure
issues.sym: The clutch pedal feels soft or sticks to the floor, the car is hard to shift, or brake fluid leaks near the bell housing or under the dash. (Manual Coupes.)
issues.why: The hydraulic clutch slave and master cylinders are among the most-reported Coupe repairs.
issues.next: Check the brake/clutch fluid reservoir. If the pedal sinks or fluid is leaking, have the clutch hydraulics replaced and bled.

issues.t: Water leaks into tail lights
issues.sym: Fog or water pooled inside the tail lights or third brake light, and sometimes bulbs or LEDs failing. (Coupe.)
issues.why: The tail light and third brake light housings and seals can let water in.
issues.next: Have the lamp seals checked and replaced. Wet lamps can corrode wiring and should be fixed early.

issues.t: Keyless door handle sensor stops working
issues.sym: The door does not lock or unlock when you touch the handle with the smart key nearby. (Coupe.)
issues.why: The proximity sensor or button in the door handle fails; it is one of the most-reported Coupe repairs.
issues.next: Use the key fob buttons in the meantime and have the handle sensor diagnosed and replaced.
